yarn 1.22.22 takes them directly, composer 2.9.5 after --.
Suites: src/. Each *-list file is the stdout of that runner's list command
(*-units files, added 2026-10-25 on node v22.23.4: the unit listing under
its working-directory prelude, the capture directory written as /fixture)
(jest and mocha JSON reduced to the fields the parsers read).
Each *-fail, *-suitefail, *-loadfail and *-hookfail file is stdout+stderr of
the runner's DEFAULT command on src/fail, not a TTY, as the jail runs it;
minitest 5.20.0.

gotestsum 1.13.0 (go install), PHP 8.5.4,
cargo 1.90.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.148 (cd1d6d546 2026-10-07).
*-help files are each runner's --help; libtest-help.txt is a cargo-built test binary's.
cargo-units-jail.txt (added 2026-10-25, cargo 1.90.0): the cargo-units.txt
listing from a clean target dir with stderr on the same stream, as the jail
returns a run's output; cargo's Compiling/Finished lines sit between its
JSON messages.
*-units-multi*.txt (added 2026-10-27; jest 30.5.2, vitest 3.2.7, node v22.23.4,
rspec-core 3.13.6, PHPUnit 11.5.57, go1.26.10, gotestsum 1.13.0, cargo 1.90.0,
cargo-nextest 0.9.148): each row's multi-unit command for units a and b of
three (src/units/multi; Go's units/gomod under -tags extra; the cargo
workspace), as "# argv:" the operator's command, "$ " the command run, then
its stdout+stderr with timings and run ids removed. Run with the agent
variables unset: jest 30 prints only its summary when it sees one.
vitest5-fail.txt, vitest5-fail-projects.txt and vitest5-fail-projects-nocolor.txt
(added 2026-10-31, vitest 5.0.3 on node v24.22.1, captured by hand, not by

HOME, LANG only, as the jail sets them), not a TTY; -projects with
vitest.projects.config.mjs as vitest.config.mjs, -nocolor with NO_COLOR=1.
vitest 5 colours its output with no TTY and no colour variable, which is
how a jailed run returns it; $DIR, ms timings, start time and duration
replaced.

Re-capture 2026-11-15: every file the script writes was re-captured on
vitest 5.1.0 and mocha 12.0.3 (jest unchanged at 30.5.2), node v22.23.5,
go1.26.11, cargo 1.90.0, cargo-nextest 0.9.148, rspec-core 3.13.6, PHPUnit
11.5.57. The runners are installed from scripts/npm-pins/runner-fixtures
by npm ci. Dates in the notes above are when each file was first added;
the hand-captured vitest5-* and *-version.txt files were not re-captured.
swift-*.txt and toolchain-swift-version.txt (added 2026-11-19; Swift version 6.3.2 (swift-6.3.2-RELEASE),
Target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu): scripts/capture-runner-fixtures.sh
through a container of corral-swift-spike run as the invoking user, on src/swift, whose test targets are CalcTests (swift-testing, five tests) and
CalcXCTests (XCTest, three, in class AdderTests). swift-list.txt is the stdout
of `swift test list`; swift-units.txt the stdout of `swift package describe
--type json` under the unit-listing prelude, the capture directory written as
/fixture; every other file is stdout+stderr, not a TTY, with the capture
directory written as $DIR. swift-fail-testing.txt and swift-fail-xctest.txt
are `swift test` with CORRAL_FAIL_TESTING or CORRAL_FAIL_XCTEST set, which
the fixture reads to plant its failures; swift-build-fail.txt is `swift test`
after a line that does not compile was appended to Sources/Calc/Calc.swift.
swift-build-target-*.txt are the compile check's `swift build --target`:
of a test target, of the source target, of a test target while a sibling
test target did not compile (with a scratch path of its own), and of a test
target after a line that does not compile was appended to the source.
swift-authored-wrapped.txt runs the two files under
src/swift-authored/wrapped, copied into the test targets, and
swift-authored-collision.txt builds CalcTests with
src/swift-authored/collision's file copied into it. swift-shapes-list.txt is
the stdout of `swift test list` with src/swift-authored/shapes's file copied
into CalcTests.
swift-single-*.txt, swift-filter-dollar.txt, swift-units-*.txt,
swift-build-target-*.txt and swift-authored-*.txt open with
`# argv:` (the operator's command, `-` for corral's own compile check)
and `$ ` (the command corral builds) and end with `# exit:` (its exit status). swift-testing runs its tests in
parallel, so the order of its lines differs between captures.
swift-codecov.json is the `llvm-cov export -format=text -summary-only`,
by the toolchain's own llvm-cov, of the profiles one `swift test
--enable-code-coverage --scratch-path <package>/.build/corral-coverage` run
of ../coverage/swift (named with --package-path) wrote, over every product
carrying a coverage map, as swiftPlugin.CoverageCmd makes it; the capture
directory written as /fixture.
The swift-build-target-*.txt, swift-authored-*.txt and
swift-shapes-list.txt files come from a later --swift-only run of the same
script on the same toolchain (2026-11-19); that run's other Swift captures
were not kept, because swift-testing's parallel order differs between runs
and the committed ones are what the tests were written against.
swift-codecov.json comes from a --swift-coverage-only run of the same
script on 2026-11-20, through a container of swift:6.3.2-noble (Swift 6.3.2,
whose default build system is native) run as the invoking user with the
network off. It replaced the export SwiftPM itself wrote, captured
2026-11-19, when swiftPlugin.CoverageCmd stopped reading that export (under
swiftbuild it covered one test product) and began merging the profiles and
exporting them over every product itself. The same run through
swift:6.4.2-resolute (Swift 6.4.2, swiftbuild by default), in a scratch copy
of the repository and not committed, wrote an export with this file's four
project files and the same per-file line counts; its other entries are the
test runner sources SwiftPM generates under .build, which the reducer skips,
and they differ between the two build systems.

HAND MEASUREMENTS, 2026-11-19 (not captures)
These are not fixtures. They are the commands behind figures that tracked
files cite with this date; their raw output is not committed and no test
reads them. Each figure is stated where it is cited, and only there. All ran
on one 32-core Linux workstation. A full run of this script rewrites this
file from its own text, which does not carry this section.

Swift runs used Swift 6.3.2 in the Docker image corral-swift-spike (Ubuntu
24.04), the image the Swift captures above came from. taplin/Lariat was
cloned at be0c5fdc9e046b529bff2b588bf4cc2c32a2ff8a with
  git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/taplin/Lariat.git
into a scratch directory $S, and swift was run as
  SW="docker run --rm -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e HOME=/tmp -v $S:$S -w $S/lariat corral-swift-spike swift"

- The rebuild probe (lang.PerRunBuilder's comment in internal/lang/lang.go):
  `$SW build --build-tests` after each change to
  Sources/LassoParser/Evaluator.swift (rewritten with its own bytes; a
  `// corral rebuild probe` line appended at the end; the same line put
  first; a one-line mutant, the `trim` case returning `.string(value)`),
  timed by SwiftPM's own "Build complete!" line.
- Whole runs (adequacy.mutantTimeoutCap's comment, and the CHANGELOG entry
  on each Swift mutant's time limit): `$SW test`, timed by /usr/bin/time
  (container start included), after `$SW build --build-tests` had settled
  the tree, with the file rewritten unchanged, with the leading comment, and
  with the same mutant.
- The coverage build's own scratch path (internal/lang/swift_coverage.go):
  in a scratch copy of the clone, `swift package resolve` once with the
  network on, then, with --network none, in this order: `swift build
  --build-tests`; `swift test --enable-code-coverage`; `swift build
  --build-tests` again; and the same with the coverage run given
  `--scratch-path .build/corral-coverage`. The notes give these steps and
  their times; the two shell scripts that ran them were not kept.
- The llvm-cov reducer reading Lariat's export (internal/lang/llvmcov.go):
  the notes give the export's size and the times under mawk and gawk, but
  not the command that timed them.
- Rust (the rebuild-floor exemption for rust in internal/lang/parity.go):
  `cargo test --lib --no-run`, cargo 1.90.0, outside the sandbox, on
  regex-syntax 0.8.5 copied from ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/regex-syntax-0.8.5
  into a scratch directory, after each change to src/hir/translate.rs,
  timed by cargo's own Finished line.
- Free dry runs of corral on the Lariat clone (docs/corral/evidence-pairing.md,
  the run-cache and evidence-promotion exemptions for swift in
  internal/lang/parity.go, and the CHANGELOG): corral built from
  feat/swift-lang in an image of corral-swift-spike plus Go 1.26.11, run with
  --network none, HOME and every corral state path in the scratch directory,
  timed with bash's `time`:
    corral certify --repo . --dry-run --evidence --substrate workspace -- swift test
    corral certify --repo . --dry-run --evidence --substrate workspace --no-selection-cache -- swift test
    corral tests map --repo-dir . --substrate workspace --out <file> -- swift test
  The files executed under Sources/LassoParser come from the tests map. The
  counts of files recorded evidence-pairing-not-built and no-paired-test
  come from the dry run's --json output (excluded_by_reason); the notes give
  the counts and not the exact --json invocation.
